subject: Renewal economics — request to revisit committed tiering & temporary price hold
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha@peregrine.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal economics — request to revisit committed tiering & temporary price hold

Hi Jasmine,

We’re starting renewal planning for our Redwood contract (term ends Jan 31) and want to discuss both an uplift to committed capacity and a short-term price hold. Long story short: forecasted ML inference demand looks like a 2.5x increase next year with a concentrated spike in Q4 (Black Friday + new feature rollout).

Two asks up front:
- Can you share a practical renewal structure that lets us increase committed throughput for 12 months but protects us from near-term price moves for the first 3 months?
- We’ll likely need a small onboarding credit to offset migration work for the expanded routes.

I’m copying Tom (procurement) — we can loop legal once we have commercial terms. I attached a brief forecast for context.

Thanks,
Samantha Cole
VP Engineering, Peregrine Analytics
Attachments: peregrine_forecast_nov2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: (internal)
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal economics — request to revisit committed tiering & temporary price hold

Rishi / Karthik — forwarding Peregrine's ask. Forecast attached. Their main asks: committed uplift for next 12 months, temporary 3-month price hold, and a small onboarding credit.

Can you:
- Recommend a commercial structure we can propose (percent uplift + credit amount + any guardrails for overages)?
- Confirm whether we can do a 3-month fixed-rate hold on hosted pricing (legal/cash implications)?

Goal: get a proposed term sheet to Samantha by EOD Wednesday so their procurement can start internal routing.

Thanks — Jasmine
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: peregrine_forecast_nov2027.xlsx (from customer)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal economics — request to revisit committed tiering & temporary price hold

Jasmine — quick initial proposal based on forecast:

Summary proposal (internal):
- 12-month renewal, increase committed tokens/throughput by 20% (year-1 committed band).
- Temporary price hold: freeze current hosted per-token rate for first 90 days post-amendment.
- One-time onboarding credit: $25,000 applied against first invoice to cover routing/ops work.
- Overage treatment: provide a capped burst-pool rate (20% premium over committed rate) for unexpected spikes; overage invoices prorated monthly.
- Safeguard: if actual usage > 160% of forecasted monthly average for 3 consecutive months, revert to standard pay-as-you-go rates for any new usage beyond the conditional uplift.

Financial note: this reduces near-term unit revenue but secures a higher committed baseline; roughly ~7% ARR headwind in year-1 versus list if they fully utilize uplift, offset by predictable commit.

I’ve drafted a term sheet (see peregrine_term_sheet_v1.pdf). Legal should be able to turn around an amendment + PO-friendly DocuSign within 48 hours once customer gives verbal.

Thoughts? If we agree, I can send this to Samantha with the term sheet and HubSpot link.

—Rishi
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: peregrine_term_sheet_v1.pdf

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha@peregrine.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Keller <tom.keller@peregrine.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 11:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed renewal summary & next steps (term sheet attached)

Hi Samantha (and Tom),

Thanks for the forecast — we discussed internally and have a proposal that tries to balance predictability for Peregrine with operational guardrails. High-level:

- Commit: 12 months, +20% committed throughput (gives you reserved capacity for the expected growth).
- Price hold: we’ll freeze your current hosted per-token rates for the first 90 days after the amendment effective date.
- Credit: one-time $25k onboarding credit applied to your first invoice to offset integration/ops work.
- Overage: access to a "burst pool" at a defined premium (20% over your committed rate) for spikes; invoiced monthly.
- Safety: a simple trigger (3 months >160% of forecast) moves incremental consumption to PAYG rates beyond the uplift.

I attached the term sheet (peregrine_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and your forecast for reference. If this looks reasonable, can we get a quick verbal ok by Friday so legal can prepare an amendment/DocuSign?

DocuSign (term sheet draft): https://www.docusign.com/containers/term-sheet/DL-7832
HubSpot deal (internal tracking): https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7832

Let me know any commercial tweaks you need — we’re happy to iterate.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 (415) 555-0123
Attachments: peregrine_term_sheet_v1.pdf, peregrine_forecast_nov2027.xlsx

From: Samantha Cole <samantha@peregrine.com>

Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@peregrine.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed renewal summary & next steps (term sheet attached)

Jasmine / Rishi — appreciate the quick work on this.

Peregrine is comfortable with the structure in principle. A couple of small asks before we route to procurement:
- Can we shift invoicing to quarterly in arrears instead of monthly? Procurement prefers a Q-invoice cadence for large multi-cloud contracts.
- Please confirm the onboarding credit appears on the first invoice and is itemized (we need that for our internal cost allocation).

I’m copying Tom (procurement). Tom — once you confirm the invoicing cadence is acceptable, we’ll route this to legal + procurement for a PO. We should be able to return a signed PO within ~5 business days.

Onward — Samantha
VP Engineering, Peregrine Analytics
